text:
B: Hello! Hello! Callum, yes? I'm Danuta.
A: Alright? Yeah, Callum. How's it going?
B: Very good, this is my last one, I'm an expert now. Have you had your tea yet?
A: Nah, not yet. My mum's cooking. I'm praying it's not salad.
B: Ha! What's wrong with salad?
A: It's not food, it's just leaves, innit. If it's salad I'm going Greggs.
B: My son Paweł says exactly this when he was young. Same face. Your photo, I said, he looks like my Paweł, but your room, oh, the wardrobe!
A: Ha, yeah, that's fair. The clothes are for selling, though. That's stock, that.
B: Stock! Very good excuse. You sell clothes?
A: Trainers mostly. On Vinted. Made forty quid on some Jordans the other week. And I'm at uni, business, second year, and I work at a pub on weekends. So I'm kind of busy, yeah?
B: Uni, very good. Your mum must be proud.
A: Yeah, she tells literally everyone. The woman at the Co-op knows. The bus driver probably knows.
B: Of course! I would do the same. What does she do, your mum?
A: She's a care assistant. Shifts and that. She's proper knackered most of the time.
B: Oh, I know this life. I'm at the hospital, I clean the wards. Early, late, early. Your mum works very hard, Callum. You help her, yes?
A: Erm... I do the bins. Sometimes. I pay board. When I remember.
B: When you remember! No, so this is what you do. Tonight, even if salad, you say "thank you, Mum, lovely". Nothing else. You'll see her face.
A: Ha, alright. Even if it's salad. That's a big ask, but alright.
B: Good boy. And where you like to go, holidays?
A: Magaluf with the lads. I wanna do somewhere in Eastern Europe, like a cheap city break. Prague or something.
B: Go to Kraków! Beautiful, cheap, the old town, and the food. Pierogi, proper ones, not from the supermarket.
A: Is it good for a night out, though?
B: Ha, yes, many students, very lively, I hear. But also you go to the castle, at least one day. Culture.
A: One day culture, rest of the time pierogi. Deal. What's a pierogi, like a pasty?
B: Little bit. Dough, and inside potato and cheese, or meat, or cabbage. I made sixty at the weekend.
A: Sixty? Mate. Right, so is it crimped on the side or the top? 'Cos a Cornish pasty, it's got to be the side, if it's on top it's a Devon one and that's just wrong.
B: You have very strong feelings about pastry!
A: Everyone in Plymouth does. It's serious, that.
B: Okay, then pierogi, the edge is on the side, all round, like little moon. So you will approve, I think—
